name: Lightning protection test joint
summary: A disconnectable joint near the base of a down-conductor that allows the earth termination to be tested separately.
description: Each down-conductor usually has a test joint at a convenient height above ground. Opening it separates the above-ground lightning conductor from the earth electrode, so electrode resistance and conductor continuity can be measured. Elevations show it as a small box or clamp mark on the down-conductor.

The test joint is not an isolating device for electrical work; it is only opened for inspection with no storm risk. The symbol does not specify clamp type or whether it is housed in a box. Missing or painted-over test joints are a common inspection finding.
readingNotes: Locate the test joint on each down-conductor.
Confirm it is reachable for inspection.
drawingChecklist: Show a test joint on every down-conductor.
Number joints to match inspection records.
distinction: A lightning test joint separates the down-conductor from its electrode; an earth test link separates the installation MET from its electrode.
